findings.observation: CLI defaults its seed to wall time; --seed hashes its exact text using djb2_hash. First lazy global engine initialization separately reads high-resolution time. Nonzero CLI seed replaces engine state, while zero is a no-op.
findings.gate_implication: Capture the resolved nonzero integer seed and actual post-initialization capsule, build/content/options identity and initialization order. Do not equate the raw --seed string or saved world seed with all draw state.
findings.next_change: Use the existing explicit seed interface before reviewed game initialization; retain zero/reseed semantics and the normal cache in the reference build.

findings.observation: The current adapter exposes the authoritative minstd_rand0 engine and six persistent rng.cpp distribution objects. It changes storage only; active original-engine build does not link the adapter.
findings.gate_implication: Existing isolated draw/capture/restore tests establish only this capsule. Full command/save/restore integration and whole-game continuation are unverified.
findings.next_change: Integrate the single overlaid rng.cpp and snapshot unit at guarded original-engine boundaries, with exact serializer ABI and floating-point build flags.

findings.observation: rng_sequence creates a complete local engine from its argument. The two snippet mt19937 engines are local; one consumes global rng_bits and the explicit-seed overload uses its argument. No independent persistent mt19937 state is declared in this inspected code.
findings.gate_implication: Do not add these stack-local engines to a quiescent capsule or call them nondeterministic merely because they use mt19937. Preserve ABI-specific algorithms, seeds, ordering and already-selected snippet IDs.
findings.next_change: Resolve snippets once in the authoritative application path and export selected IDs/parameters. Never reseed/rerun snippet selection during Rust redraw or language change.

findings.observation: Uniform, binomial and Poisson distributions are members of shared int_distribution implementations, populated from content. mutable_overmap_placement_rule owns int_distribution max and samples it during realise. They consume rng_get_engine but are outside the six-object registry.
findings.gate_implication: This audit has not inspected compiler-library internals or run continuation tests for these objects. Their lifetime is longer than one draw. Do not assert either a missing stochastic cache or statelessness without ABI-specific proof; content definitions and any implementation-specific persistent sample state must be covered.
findings.next_change: Inspect exactly the installed libc++ binomial/Poisson/uniform implementations and verify hot-object continuation across fresh content reload. If state persists beyond parameters, add stable definition-keyed transactional distribution-state capture; otherwise retain source/ABI/content binding and the proof.

findings.observation: Shrapnel hit counts, field decay initialization and seasonal wind direction use local distributions directly on the global engine. These are real gameplay calls. Their local distribution lifetimes end before the proposed completed-command checkpoint.
findings.gate_implication: The engine capsule includes draws through rng_get_engine even if they bypass rng() wrappers; no extra surviving local engine was found here. Same libc++ ABI, parameters, draw order and command-boundary scope are still required.
findings.next_change: Include these mechanics in real-engine continuation scenarios. Do not replace their algorithms with one of the six helper distributions.

findings.observation: Twenty inventoried std::shuffle sites pass rng_get_engine. The twenty-first shuffle is the separate SDL playlist engine. Standard-library shuffle draw algorithms are target-specific.
findings.gate_implication: Global-engine capture covers their mutable engine, not cross-library sequence portability. Container order must be preserved for a specific demonstrated path; this inventory makes no generic container nondeterminism claim.
findings.next_change: Keep exact target ABI/content and compare source-backed shuffled world/item outcomes in the real engine; preserve actual input order rather than sorting every container.

findings.observation: Animated weather input waiting draws global rng for candidate drop coordinates before visibility filtering, and repeats on native timeouts. This is the already-confirmed rain blocker.
findings.gate_implication: An action-only trace cannot reproduce the unmodified feature-enabled reference RNG sequence. Pure observation getters must never enter this wait/draw path.
findings.next_change: First record native event/timeout/viewport traces. The user-authorized cosmetic RNG separation must be an explicit overlay with reference-sequence differences and gameplay-rule comparison; animation-disabled tests alone do not prove the release path.

findings.observation: The WEATHER case reads global rng_bits while drawing a tile. This executes before the later fg/bg variant-count check, so a tileset with only one sprite does not remove this draw.
findings.gate_implication: Rain-coordinate isolation alone leaves tile drawing able to advance gameplay RNG. The source comment about not needing determinism is not an isolated engine.
findings.next_change: Use explicit cosmetic state/phase or an already-selected sprite in the immutable render record; include weather sprite drawing in full-engine render/RNG neutrality checks.

findings.observation: ASCII overmap drawing performs reservoir-style NPC color selection using global one_in when different-color NPCs/followers share a tile. Both loops are inside the blink/overlay-enabled draw branch.
findings.gate_implication: Repeated overmap redraw can consume global RNG without a gameplay command for an actual populated-map condition. A tile-only weather fix does not cover ASCII windows.
findings.next_change: Prepare the color once from a cosmetic engine or stable visible-NPC identities, and export the chosen visible color. Preserve information visibility and document native visual/reference RNG differences.

findings.observation: Tiled overmap debug monster-group overlay randomly chooses a representative with the global engine. It is guarded by draw_overlays and overmap_debug_mongroup, not by SDL_SOUND or Android.
findings.gate_implication: This is compiled debug-feature presentation, distinct from ordinary overmap color selection; preserve/support it or document its remaining purity gap. No claim that normal gameplay always enters this branch.
findings.next_change: Use cosmetic representative selection in the explicit debug render snapshot and add a feature-enabled test.

findings.observation: A cache miss in displayed overmap weather calls get_weather_conditions(location,time,seed), then get_weather. Despite const, it draws global RNG for wind and changes static current_winddir. Native save serializes weather_manager.winddirection, not weather_generator.current_winddir. All lexical current_winddir references in scope are in weather_gen.cpp/h.
findings.gate_implication: RNG capsule equality alone does not restore this separate wind-history state. Preview call order/cache hits can affect later wind calculation. Manager winddirection is not a demonstrated substitute: overrides and forecast calls can separate it from the static generator state.
findings.next_change: Add versioned authoritative auxiliary-state capture/restore for current_winddir, with source-bound range/compatibility validation, after successful native reconstruction. Split reviewed UI preview production from authoritative weather evolution; do not call get_weather as a pure observer or alter simulation wind rules wholesale. Audit the UI cache lifetime when comparing native traces.

findings.observation: Scrolling combat text chooses non-HP directions using global one_in when ANIMATION_SCT is enabled. test_mode returns before these draws. These draws occur when messages are added, rather than every redraw.
findings.gate_implication: A fixture with test_mode or SCT disabled omits actual source consumption. Animation options currently change subsequent gameplay RNG ordering.
findings.next_change: Isolate only the reviewed direction-choice cosmetics and freeze chosen direction in the presentation event. Include enabled SCT in real gameplay reference comparisons.

findings.observation: A portal-storm distraction query selects a random popup color from the global engine and also marks activity distractions ignored. The color is cosmetic; the whole function is not pure presentation.
findings.gate_implication: Do not move the complete query into a redraw getter or remove its gameplay side effects while isolating its color draw.
findings.next_change: Keep activity mutations in the original application flow, select cosmetic color once, and export an owned prompt event.

findings.observation: Snippet expansion, punctuation tags and dynamic-line selection may draw while producing dialogue text. Some are called from menu construction and narrative effects. They cannot be rerun safely by a Rust locale formatter.
findings.gate_implication: Semantic-ID migration must retain selected branch/snippet/punctuation identity and evaluated parameters. Locale changes may affect recursive expansion if selection is performed after translation in the reference path; do not claim whole-game RNG independence from merely translating JSON.
findings.next_change: Use source-bound IDs for preselected narrative variants, carry immutable evaluated parameters and external-name literals, and compare actual engine draw counts before/after redraw and language switches.

findings.observation: TURN_DURATION is an unguarded general option defaulting to 0 (turn-based, realtime progression disabled), range 0..10, step 0.05. Its actual native input/action bodies are listed in the browser build, without a native-OS exclusion. Only a value > 0.005 converts elapsed milliseconds to additional move cost and permits idle timeout progression; non-timeout actions subtract that cost. Separately, blocking-activity key checks are rate-limited by steady-clock reads even in default mode. The resulting ACTION_TIMEOUT pauses the player only when check_safe_mode_allowed(false) succeeds; preserve Safe Mode behavior.
findings.gate_implication: The timed gameplay effect is optional user-enabled behavior, not the default fresh profile. A persisted profile can override it; this source audit did not run the browser or read user profiles. Equal key sequences and RNG state are insufficient for the enabled option when elapsed timings differ.
findings.next_change: Retain the option and record/replay clock-derived move costs and polling decisions as explicit platform inputs. Test default zero and enabled realtime profiles separately; default-mode success does not prove all-option determinism.

findings.observation: Tile animation phase and minimap blinking use real clock values; monster visual variant seed uses a native pointer address, while graffiti/player seeds use std::hash<string>. These are visual-selection inputs in the inspected functions, not evidence of independent simulation entropy.
findings.gate_implication: Pure rendering of a copied frame must freeze explicit phase and resolved variant IDs. The same saved world across new runtimes can choose different monster sprite variants even with equal gameplay RNG, due to pointer identity.
findings.next_change: Export the selected variant/animation phase for initial draw-backend work. A later semantic renderer needs stable visible entity IDs and a defined hash; document the visual fidelity decision without translating external names.

findings.observation: Native character JSON persists simulation calendar and gameplay records. Master JSON persists game::seed, assigned from a global draw at start_game. The inspected save serializers have no global engine/distribution stream capture or rng_set_engine_seed restore. The world/weather seed is not the current minstd engine state or normal cache.
findings.gate_implication: A complete native file export alone is not deterministic RNG resume. Conversely simulation calendar is source-persisted game state and must not be normalized away as a platform timestamp.
findings.next_change: Capture native complete file set, authoritative auxiliary state and the full RNG capsule together at one guarded boundary; validate source/build/content/serializer identity and atomic generation commit.

findings.observation: Monster load initializes any newly missing special-attack cooldown by RNG. game::load emits game_load, activates passives, loads existing-character EOCs and rebuilds caches. Event EOCs may activate for any configured required_event; this audit does not scan data to assert which defaults or mods bind game_load/save.
findings.gate_implication: Native reconstruction can consume draws and mutate world state before resume. Restoring the capsule before load is insufficient; restoring it after load cannot undo world mutations caused by incompatible content or event logic.
findings.next_change: Use a candidate runtime, exact compatible content and reviewed load semantics. Restore auxiliary state and RNG after successful reconstruction, before resumed native computation, then prove real continuation. Preserve or explicitly model load events rather than skipping them.

findings.observation: Autosave defaults on, at 50 simulation turns and at least 5 real minutes, both conditions required. save() emits an event containing elapsed and total real playtime before file writes; game_over carries total playtime. Stats/event records preserve such values and configured event EOCs can observe them. No data/mod scan establishes a particular active EOC binding.
findings.gate_implication: Real playtime is an observable native event input, not automatically disposable file metadata. Save is not a pure read and an event can be emitted even if later native file writing fails.
findings.next_change: Record/inject clock-derived event payloads and save-trigger schedule for replay. Define narrow comparison normalization only for proven platform metadata; capture RNG after original save-event semantics and check late failures do not replace prior durable checkpoints.

references.anchor: Dummy implementations for builds without sound

findings.observation: SDL playlist has a separate persistent clock-seeded engine; sound-variant/pitch paths also draw global RNG. Those implementation bodies are inactive in the current build, whose flags omit SDL_SOUND. However weather_sound passes random_direction() to an unguarded call; arguments are evaluated even for the compiled no-op sound stub. Hearing/message probabilities in that function remain gameplay behavior.
findings.gate_implication: SOUND=0 does not imply that all audio-related source call sites consume zero global RNG. Future audio adapter determinism must distinguish media cosmetics from retained hearing simulation.
findings.next_change: Keep omitted audio scope explicit. When implementing audio, use platform-owned cosmetic random state for playlist/pitch and isolate reviewed direction-only draws, while preserving audible-message/hearing rules and exact reference differences.

findings.observation: Sound clustering drives monster AI; deafening/pain, awakening and uncertain sound-marker locations use gameplay RNG outside SDL_SOUND. Marker randomness governs player information rather than merely audio output.
findings.gate_implication: Do not relocate every sound/marker RNG to a cosmetic stream or remove sound mechanics because the audio backend is disabled.
findings.next_change: Keep these original gameplay algorithms and include hearing/marker outcomes in deterministic continuation; Rust renders the already-chosen permitted marker positions.

findings.observation: The four rand/random lexical occurrences resolve to a math parser wrapper calling rng and an om_direction helper calling rng, including declarations/call sites. rand_char is declared/defined but no source call site was found in this scoped tree. Clock-pattern matches also include e.time() and a consumption_event member initializer, which are not real-clock calls.
findings.gate_implication: No actual libc rand/srand, OS entropy call or random_device was found in this lexical scope. This is bounded negative evidence, not proof over excluded third-party/generated/platform implementations or a compiled AST.
findings.next_change: Retain unclassified matches in the raw inventory, review new source/build versions, and keep compile guards/context in subsequent audits.

findings.observation: World timestamps/archive file times/graveyard names are metadata; perf/debug timings are diagnostics; recipe search and pathfinding clocks schedule progress/cancel opportunities. Android SDL touch timing and MinGW fallback thread clocks occur in separately guarded paths. This audit does not infer simulation nondeterminism from every timer or container.
findings.gate_implication: Replay input-cancellation and progress-induced native redraw side effects where exercised. Normalize only demonstrated metadata when comparing equivalent world state; do not classify Android-only touch timers as browser paths.
findings.next_change: Use source-bound clock categories and accepted-event receipts. Keep platform metadata separately versioned where needed for exact file export/source fidelity.

findings.observation: current_winddir is a concrete gap, not a complete auxiliary-state census. weather_precise, wind_direction_override, windspeed_override and weather_override are not serialized in the displayed native weather serializer; update_weather reads the overrides. get_weather_conditions(w) temporarily overwrites weather_precise to evaluate content conditions, restoring it on normal return. Overmap weather_cache and last_weather_display are process-static, so cache-hit lifetime also affects whether RNG-consuming calculation runs.
findings.gate_implication: Do not declare a complete weather checkpoint after capturing only current_winddir. Distinguish authoritative overrides/history from derived caches and prove each reconstruction rule; this audit does not assert every cached field must be serialized.
findings.next_change: Extend the auxiliary-state review and versioned schema with semantically necessary overrides/history. Validate derived reconstruction without additional unintended draws, and compare fresh candidate-runtime versus existing-runtime cache behavior. Never invoke condition evaluation as a passive observer.
